channels.heading: Channels
channels.intro: Where to send notifications outside the app. Channels are yours — they work in all your households, and you choose below what goes to them.
channels.emptyBody: Notifications reach the bell in the app anyway. A channel adds email, ntfy push, Telegram, Matrix or a webhook.
channels.testOk: Test sent — check that the message arrived.
channels.deleteBody: Channel {{name}} will disappear from all preferences, and notifications not yet sent to it will be lost.

dialog.unsupportedType: This server doesn't support channels of type {{type}}.
dialog.addedToast: Channel {{name}} added. Send a test to check that it works.
dialog.typeFixed: Type: {{type}} — the channel type can't be changed.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.nameHint: E.g. “Phone (ntfy)” — this is the channel's name in preferences.
dialog.enabledHint: A disabled channel gets no notifications but stays in preferences.
dialog.secretChangeHint: Enter a new value — it replaces the saved one.
dialog.secretRemoveHint: The channel will work without a secret.
dialog.noMasterKey: The server has no DENAR_MASTER_KEY, so it won't store a secret. Ask your administrator to set the key.
dialog.secretNote: We encrypt the secret on the server and never show it — not even to you.

url.label: URL
url.hint: Denar will POST the JSON of every notification here.

secret.label: Signing secret
secret.hint: Optional. With it, every request has an X-Denar-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256).

topic.label: Topic
topic.hint: Letters, digits, “-” and “_”. On a public server pick one that's hard to guess.

chat_id.label: chat_id
chat_id.hint: Chat number (groups start with a minus) or @channel_name.

room_id.label: Room ID
room_id.hint: The internal room ID (starts with “!”), not a #room alias.

access_token.label: Access token
access_token.hint: Token of the account that posts to the room (ideally a separate bot account).

typeDescription.webhook: JSON POST to your service (n8n, Home Assistant, your own server)
typeDescription.ntfy: Push notifications to your phone via ntfy
typeDescription.telegram: A message from your bot on Telegram
typeDescription.matrix: A message in a Matrix room (Element)

email.p1: The Denar server sends messages through the configured SMTP. Check your spam folder after the first test.

webhook.p1: Every notification is a POST with a JSON body: id, type, title, body, url, household {id, name}, occurred_at and data.
webhook.p2: With a secret, the request has an X-Denar-Signature: sha256=<hex> header, where <hex> is the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body computed with the secret. Compare it on your side before trusting the body.
webhook.p3: X-Denar-Event is the event type and X-Denar-Delivery the delivery ID (retries share it, so duplicates are easy to drop).

ntfy.p1: Install the ntfy app and subscribe to the same topic on the same server.
ntfy.p2: On your own ntfy server with access control, enter the token of a user who can publish to the topic.

telegram.p1: Create a bot with @BotFather and copy its token.
telegram.p2: Send anything to your bot (or add it to a group), then open https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getUpdates — chat_id is the message.chat.id field.

matrix.p1: Invite the account whose token you enter to the room and accept the invitation.
matrix.p2: You'll find the room ID in Element: Room settings → Advanced → Internal room ID.
